findings.quote: Start from `units/ogre.json` (lower-left, a club, no shield) or `units/hyborem.json` (lower-left, a greatsword, no shield), whatever your unit's facing; `facing` and the joints are what change.
findings.evidence: Both files carry `beats` overrides written for a lower-left unit (units/ogre.json strike 3-5 'toward the lower-left', flinch 0 'hit from the lower-left ... toward the upper-right', death 4-5 'upper-right' / 'feet toward the lower-left'; hyborem.json strike 4, flinch 0 and death 5 the same). recipe.py:196-202 `beat_text` returns an override exactly as written. Only the default texts go through `swap_sides`, and only when the set is mirrored. Test: a copy of ogre.json with only `facing` set to lower-right printed 'pose set near, smear cw' (lower-right guides), but its strike 3/4/5 and flinch 0 'own' texts still say lower-left / upper-right. For a club unit no prop gets flagged, so 1d gives no hint that these texts need rewriting. The model would get guides that strike lower-right and text that says lower-left.
findings.fix: "Start from `units/ogre.json` or `units/hyborem.json` (both look lower-left). Besides `facing` and the joints, change `name`, `sprite`, `description`, `hands`, `scale`, `head_r` and `limb`. For a lower-right unit, rewrite every copied `beats` override with left and right swapped. Overrides go to the model exactly as written and are never mirrored (recipe.py `beat_text`)."

findings.where: Before you start, 'The sprite' (line 83); Round B paragraph (lines 365-366)
findings.quote: An M7 unit PNG at most 128 px wide and 128 px tall, feet 2 px above the bottom ... / both sets were re-cut from the same picks, so every frame touches the ground
findings.evidence: No code checks the feet margin. load_unit (recipe.py:74) puts the PNG's bottom row on canvas row 127. slice_sheet snaps every redrawn frame's lowest row to row 125 (sheet.py ground snap -> ak.snap_ground, target ANCHOR[1]-1). unit_hyborem.png (105x120) has 4 empty rows under the feet (lowest opaque row 115). So in final_hyborem the frames built from the sprite (idle 0-3, strike 0 and 7, flinch 3) end on row 123, and the redrawn frames end on row 125: a 2 px drop at strike 0->1, a rise at 6->7 and a rise at flinch 2->3 (measured on the committed frames). A round B judge flagged it: 'The rest pose sits 2px higher than the action frames (feet at y123 vs 125)' (round_b.json, hyborem_new strike). So the guide's own worked example breaks its sprite requirement, and the sentence 'every frame touches the ground' is not quite true for it.
findings.fix: In 'The sprite': "feet exactly 2 px above the bottom (the lowest opaque row is the PNG's third row from the bottom). The recipe does not check this. With more empty rows, the redrawn frames land lower than the idle (Hyborem has 4, so his strike drops 2 px on frame 1)." In round B: "so every redrawn frame now touches the ground row (Hyborem's sprite-based frames sit 2 px above it, because his PNG has 4 empty rows under the feet)".

findings.quote: an impact spark at the weapon's tip on the hit frame wherever a steel-coloured patch shows there (a blade, or a club's spikes), and a smear arc on the swing and hit frames only when a steel-coloured blade at least 20 px long shows in both frames
findings.evidence: finish.apply_strike_fx (finish.py:122-135) fires the spark whenever the hit frame has 10 or more steel-coloured pixels anywhere (finish.py:59-60). It places the spark at metrics.tip_point: the pixel of the largest steel blob that is farthest from the body centre (metrics.py:114-126). Nothing checks that this blob is the weapon or sits at its tip. Each smear is decided on its own: frame 3 needs a blade of 20 px or more in frames 2 and 3, and frame 4 needs one in frames 3 and 4 (finish.py:128-131). 'Both frames' therefore means a frame and the one before it, not the swing and hit frames. Measured results match the examples: swordsman blades 28.6/32.1/30.5 px give both smears; ogre spikes give 3-5 px blobs, so a spark (73 px changed on frame 4) but no smear; Hyborem has 0 steel px, so neither.
findings.fix: "on the strike, an impact spark on the hit frame at the outermost point of the largest steel-coloured patch in that frame (a blade, a club's spikes, or light steel armour if that is the largest patch); and a smear arc on the swing frame and on the hit frame, each drawn only when a steel-coloured blade at least 20 px long shows in that frame and in the frame before it"

findings.quote: in death 4–7 the dropped weapon is always drawn as a sword blade; that is expected, and the death texts must name your weapon so the model draws it.
findings.evidence: guides.py sword() draws every weapon from r_ha to tip as a light blade with a crossguard and grip, in every guide cell. In the ogre's guides_check.png the club is a white sword in strike 1-6, flinch 0-2 and death 1-3 too. Death 4-7 differ only in that the weapon is the source's dropped `sword`, placed where the swordsman drops his. The sentence suggests only those cells misdraw the weapon.
findings.fix: "every guide draws the weapon as a sword blade with a crossguard, whatever the unit carries, and in death 4–7 the dropped weapon lies where the swordsman drops his; that is expected, so every text that shows the weapon (the death texts especially) must name your weapon so the model draws it."

I checked the guide against lib/*.py, m7/lib/imggen.py, every unit file, both pose sets, the final_* folders, budget.json, spend.jsonl and every judging file. I ran recipe.py only with --grid, --show-beats and --check-guides, into work/fc_tmp_* folders that I then deleted. spend.jsonl stays at 76 rows and git status is clean.

What I verified as correct:

- **Commands and outputs.** Every command and flag works as described, and writes what the guide says: --grid writes a 960×768 grid.png at 6× (lines every 8 px, labels every 16) and prints (32, 8) for the swordsman, (27, 8) for Hyborem and (31, 8) for the ogre. --show-beats prints facing, pose set, smear direction, 'own' marks and shield/sword/blade flags for strike 1–6, flinch 0–2 and death 1–7; the near-set defaults leave 15 of 16 flagged. --check-guides makes the 3-row labelled sheet with red bones, yellow weapon chain and white joints, and gives the 'shortened' warning; the clamp is x 18–142, y 3–125 and the template region x 16–143, y 0–127. Also correct: --rebuild/--pick, how --anims re-rolls (death always regenerates flinch, out_1/out_2 overwritten), the preview and metrics commands, and that jitter appears only in metrics.json.
- **Output contract.** 160×128 frames, the manifest keys, hit on strike frame 4, and timings of 1000/870/440/1180 ms with loop/hold_last. Anchor (80,126) goes to tile +96,+54, and the banner is placed from the idle frame-0 bbox. Mirroring is about x=80, and the sheets are 160 px apart.
- **Unit files and pose sets.** load_unit requires facing and every joint except shield. The optional keys and their defaults are right (sharpen 3.0, defringe, palette, tag defaulting to anim/final), as are head_r 13 and limb 1.4/1.45, and 98/86 = 1.14. All four rows of the pose-set table match pose_set(): r_sh vs l_sh, far/near, mirrored.
- **Facing mechanics.** beat_text picks BEATS or BEATS_NEAR and applies swap_sides when mirrored, and the default texts point the right way. The prompt states the facing twice (now an f-string, with a guard against leftover braces). Lower-right guides are drawn mirrored via the pose's facing key. smear_direction is ccw for far, cw for near, flipped when mirrored. The vignette has A and B on one row, with the attacker on the side opposite its facing.
- **Retargeting.** rel, drawn (weapon chain ramped 15–60°) and disp (breath) behave as described. WARP_FRAMES, STANDING, x_snap, ground_limit 20/40, and floating labels above 3 px all match.
- **Review sheet.** 2×, cropped to x 16–143, with labels 'slid' and 'ground' (shown at 4 px or more) and 'FLOATS'.
- **Effects, purple, canvas, model.** The hit flash is on frame 0 of flinch and death, and the FX outcomes for the swordsman, ogre and Hyborem are as stated. The purple threshold is 1% of opaque pixels: lich 12.6%, Sheaim mage 21.8%, every other roster sprite below 0.1%. Every constant in the canvas-change list exists where the guide says; the size refusal is at 128. The model contract and the calibration claims (flare redraws the reference cell, gpt-image-2 is +19%, high quality costs 2×) are right.
- **Budget and cost.** Caps are $5/$20/$20 with an estimate of $0.2487 per call. Three calls run about 19–26 s and cost $0.234.
- **Evidence numbers.** The round 1 table matches scores.json for all eight rows. By rank, every judge put the whole-sprite tween last and the cut-out rig second to last in strike, flinch and death. Round 2 gives 7.90/7.68/7.62/7.85 against the right competitors; death is the only one ranked first by all judges (mean rank 1.0), and the idle and strike leads are 0.20 and 0.30. Near-set panel: 7.83/7.83/7.83 against 7.33 and 5.33; one assignment of judge letters reproduces the whole table, though the 'map' that panel.json's _about mentions is missing. Round A: Hyborem was read as looking lower-left, the first post-rule Hyborem set struck the wrong way, and the prompt bug and the worker dry run are recorded. I recomputed all 24 means in the round B table from round_b.json and every one matches. The direction verdicts are 3 of 3. The 22 px and 21 px floats are now snapped (build_report shows 22 and 21–22 on the picked variants). The swordsman's idle frames are byte-identical between final/ and final_swordsman/. The near-set shield moves behind the body at strike 3–5. The worked-example facings, files and legacy flags are right.

findings.quote: Start from `units/ogre.json` (lower-left, a club, no shield) or `units/hyborem.json` (lower-left, a greatsword, no shield), whatever your unit's facing; `facing` and the joints are what change.
findings.evidence: Both templates look lower-left. units/ogre.json overrides strike 3, 4, 5, flinch 0 and death 4, 5 with texts that name the lower-left or upper-right. I copied ogre.json and changed only `facing` to lower-right (scratch file, deleted since). `--show-beats` printed 'facing lower-right, pose set near, smear cw' and still sent six `own` texts saying 'steps toward the lower-left', 'smashing down-left', 'hit from the lower-left; head snaps back toward the upper-right', 'feet toward the lower-left'. Nothing in recipe.py checks the direction words in an override. beat_text() returns the override as is, and --show-beats flags only shield/sword/blade. So following 1c to the letter on a lower-right unit sends the model lower-left texts beside lower-right guides, which breaks rule 1. Rule 1 also tells the reader that 'the recipe then picks the poses, the beat texts and the prompt that strike that way'. That is not true of overridden texts, and the guide says most units need overrides (the worker needs 15 of 16). Once a text is overridden, --show-beats no longer prints the default, so the agent cannot compare the two afterwards.
findings.fix: 1c: "Start from `units/ogre.json` (lower-left, a club, no shield) or `units/hyborem.json` (lower-left, a greatsword, no shield). Replace everything unit-specific (name, sprite, description, hands, scale, head_r, limb, joints, facing) and rewrite every `beats` text. Both examples look lower-left, so their strike 3–5, flinch 0 and death 4–5 texts name the lower-left and upper-right. Copied into a lower-right unit, they tell the model to strike the wrong way, and the recipe does not catch it. Run step 1d before you write any override, so you see the defaults for your facing." At the end of rule 1, add: "The recipe picks the default texts; any text you override is yours, and it must keep the default's direction (step 1d)."

findings.quote: The sprint's judged swordsman set (`final/`) breaks this rule (he looks lower-right and strikes lower-left), so do not copy it.
findings.evidence: Only final/ is named, but every sprint set on the swordsman strikes lower-left. The hit frame (strike 4) of each arms/*/ set (A0, C, G0, G1, G2, K, R) and of final_v1_nofx/ reaches x 16-29 on the left, while the swordsman's rest pose spans x 45-113 and final_swordsman's hit frame reaches x 149 on the right. spec.md:32-33 says 'The sprint's arms and `final/` keep this section as written'. Round B judged final_nofx/, not final/, as the failing set (key R = swordsman_judged = final_nofx, 3 of 3 judges 'matches': false). README.md:66-67 puts final_hyborem_v1/, which keeps the rule (round B: T matches 3/3), in the same list as the rule-breaking swordsman sets, under 'made before the strike-direction rule'.
findings.fix: Rule 1: "The sprint's swordsman sets (`final/`, `final_nofx/`, `final_v1_nofx/`) and every method set in `arms/*/` break this rule (he looks lower-right and strikes lower-left), so do not copy any of them." README layout: "`final/` (recipe with FX), `final_nofx/`, `final_v1_nofx/` (first build): the sprint's swordsman sets, which strike away from where he looks; `final_hyborem_v1/`: the sprint's Hyborem set, which keeps the rule."

findings.quote: every new set strikes where its sprite looks (3 of 3 judges each)
findings.evidence: This holds for the direction panel (round_b.json direction.swordsman_new.matches = [true, true, true]). But the quality judges in the same round read the near-set strike differently. Judge 2 wrote 'He flips to face right on frames 3-5 and slashes behind his own facing, with the shield swapping arms, then turns back on frame 6', scored the new swordsman's strike 4.45 (quality.swordsman_new.strike = [6.7, 4.45, 7.7]) and preferred the rule-breaking set (_prefer U2:strike). In round A, judge 3 wrote 'the turn into the lunge reads almost like a flip'. The Known limits bullet reports this only as the shield vanishing or swapping arms. So the one pose set that only lower-right units use can read as a strike the wrong way, which is exactly what rule 1 exists to prevent.
findings.fix: At :353: "every new set strikes where its sprite looks (3 of 3 direction judges each; one of the three quality judges still read the new swordsman's strike frames 3–5 as turning round and slashing behind himself, see Known limits)". At the end of the near-set bullet: "...or swapping arms, and one judge per round read the turn as a facing flip. For a lower-right unit, check strike frames 3–5 for this in step 3 and step 4."

findings.quote: have judges compare them blind: letters instead of names, a frame-ordering test, and scores for motion, consistency, style and appeal (`lib/judging.py`, `JUDGE_BRIEF.md`)
findings.evidence: JUDGE_BRIEF.md:4 briefs judges on 'a chibi **swordsman** facing the lower-left'. Line 9 tells them to read beats.md, whose main tables (lines 19-52) are the far set: strike to the lower-left, corpse feet at the lower-left. A re-test run as the guide says would tell judges that a rule-following swordsman set (near set, lower-right) is a facing flip. ANIMATING_UNITS.md:69 calls beats.md 'the swordsman's frame-by-frame beat sheet'. In fact the swordsman now uses only its last section ('The lower-right (near) set', line 57). The main tables apply to lower-left units and to the rule-breaking sprint sets, and beats.md says nothing about this at the top.
findings.fix: :311: "(`lib/judging.py`; `JUDGE_BRIEF.md` is the sprint's brief: it says the swordsman faces lower-left and points judges at the far-set beat sheet, so before using it rewrite its first paragraph with the unit's real facing and strike direction and name the beat texts that apply)". :69: "`spec.md` is the contract. `beats.md` is the beat sheet: its main tables are the far set (lower-left units such as the ogre and Hyborem; the sprint's swordsman sets used them too, against rule 1), and its last section is the near set (the swordsman as he really is)."

findings.quote: spec.md: "a lower-right unit uses the near pose set (`poses_near.json`, texts in `lib/beats.py` `BEATS_NEAR`)"; README: "`poses_near.json` (from `lib/poses_near_src.py`): the pose set for units that look lower-right."
findings.evidence: recipe.pose_set() (lib/recipe.py:79-86) returns ('far', True) for a lower-right unit whose r_sh is right of l_sh. The guide's own table (ANIMATING_UNITS.md:154) has the same row: 'lower-right | right (the far hand) | far set, mirrored'. It also returns ('near', True) for a lower-left unit with the weapon on screen-right. So spec.md, which the guide calls 'the full contract', and the README contradict the table in two of its four cases. ANIMATING_UNITS.md:296 '(`poses_near.json`, lower-right)' has the same simplification.
findings.fix: spec.md: "...hits come from there, and the facing and the weapon arm's screen side pick the pose set: the near set (`poses_near.json`, texts in `BEATS_NEAR`) for a lower-right unit with the weapon in the near, screen-left hand, mirrored for a lower-left unit with it in the screen-right hand (table in `ANIMATING_UNITS.md`, step 1c)." README: "the pose set for units that look lower-right with the weapon in the near (screen-left) hand and, mirrored, for lower-left units with it in the screen-right hand." Guide :296: "(`poses_near.json`: lower-right with the weapon in the near hand, or mirrored)".

findings.quote: To make idle, strike, flinch or death animations for an M7 unit sprite, follow `projects/ffh-anim-sprint/ANIMATING_UNITS.md`.
findings.evidence: The sparse hook (projects/ffh2-rs/tools/agents/hooks/post-checkout) checks out only '/*', '/.claude/' and '/projects/ffh2-rs/', so in an agent worktree this path does not exist. The light fix, `git sparse-checkout add projects/ffh-anim-sprint`, appears only on ANIMATING_UNITS.md:8-9, inside the file the agent cannot open yet. The root section beneath only says `git sparse-checkout disable`, which checks out the whole tree (about 200 MB per the hook comment). I reproduced the hook's non-cone patterns in a scratch repo (git 2.43, deleted since): `git sparse-checkout add projects/ffh-anim-sprint` returned 0 and checked out the folder.
findings.fix: Append to the root 'Unit animations' paragraph: "In a sparse agent worktree that folder is not checked out; run `git sparse-checkout add projects/ffh-anim-sprint` first."

findings.quote: Archers and casters need their own beat sheet and poses (a draw-and-release or a cast, in `lib/poses_src.py`, `lib/poses_near_src.py` and `lib/beats.py`).
findings.evidence: Those files hold the one far set and the one near set, and every melee unit uses them (recipe.SETS, recipe.beat_text). Writing a cast there would replace the swing for the ogre, Hyborem and the swordsman. The tools have no body-plan selector. The only hook is the `poses_from` key (recipe.unit_poses), which the guide at :125 says to 'leave out'. With `poses_from`, the file is still mirrored by pose_set(), so it must be written in that set's convention, and all 16 beat texts must be overridden. The guide also never says whether an agent asked to animate a caster (roster: lich, Sheaim mage, priest of leaves) should stop or use the melee strike.
findings.fix: "Archers and casters have no poses yet. A cast or shot needs a new pose file in the `poses.json` schema, written for the set that `--show-beats` names for the unit (the far set's lower-left/far-hand convention or the near set's lower-right/near-hand one; the recipe mirrors it as needed). Point the unit file's `poses_from` at it, override all 16 beat texts, and aim the cast or shot toward the facing (rule 1). Do not edit `lib/poses_src.py`, `lib/poses_near_src.py` or `lib/beats.py` for this: every melee unit uses them. This is untested; if you were not asked to build it, say so instead of animating a caster with the melee strike."

findings.quote: It came out of a blind bake-off of seven methods in October 2026: after fixes, it had the top mean score in all four animations in a second blind round against the strongest of the others (evidence at the end).
findings.evidence: The round-2 win (judging/verify_scores.json: final_nofx 7.90/7.68/7.62/7.85) was for the swordsman set that strikes away from where he looks (round_b.json: swordsman_judged = final_nofx, matches false, 3 of 3). The recipe as now documented has a new near set, the 'drawn'/'disp' retarget, the sideways snap, interior de-fringe and the 40 px ground snap, and it was compared blind only with its own earlier sets (round A and round B quality pairs), never with the other methods. Of the round-B re-cuts that replaced the two clear losses, the doc itself says 'not judged again'. The details are further down, but the opening claim reads as if it covers the current method.
findings.fix: "It came out of a blind bake-off of seven methods on the swordsman in October 2026: after fixes, it had the top mean score in all four animations in a second blind round against the strongest of the others. Those sets predate rule 1. The recipe as it stands now (rule 1, the near set, the later fixes) has been compared blind only with its own earlier sets (evidence at the end)."

findings.quote: the other hand is `l_ha`, and the `hands` sentence says that it holds the shaft lower down at rest (the poses swing one-handed)
findings.evidence: The prompt repeats the `hands` sentence for every cell (recipe.prompt), while the guides move the free hand away: far-set strike 2 'tucked in', strike 4 'swung back for balance' (beats.py). The round-A dry run on the worker (judging/post_rule/round_a.json, dry.findings[0]) asked for the overrides to say whether the free hand lets go, and for a two-handed worked example. Neither is in the guide, yet :351 says the dry-run gaps 'are all fixed'. No two-handed unit has been generated: the worker only ran to step 1e.
findings.fix: After '(the poses swing one-handed)': "so in `hands` and in every override that mentions the free hand, say that it lets go during the swing and is an empty fist (strike 2–5, flinch 0–1, death 1–3), or the model gets a text and a guide that disagree. No two-handed unit has been generated yet; check the strike closely in step 3." At :351, change 'All are fixed' to 'All but the two-handed example are addressed'.

findings.quote: **magenta or purple specks** on outlines or seams (the recipe recolours most of them);
findings.evidence: recipe.prepare() de-fringes only when finish.defringe_applicable(base) holds, that is, when under 1% of the sprite's opaque pixels are purplish (lib/finish.py:149-154). For the lich (12.6%) and the Sheaim mage (21.8%) it does nothing, so for purple-art units the recipe recolours none of the specks. Known limits says de-fringe turns off but not that step 3's reassurance stops applying, and it gives no instruction for such a unit.
findings.fix: "**magenta or purple specks** on outlines or seams (the recipe recolours most of them, but not for purple-art units such as the lich or the Sheaim mage, where de-fringing is off and every speck stays: pick the cleanest variant and re-roll if both have specks)"

findings.quote: in death 4–7 the dropped weapon is always drawn as a sword blade; that is expected, and the death texts must name your weapon so the model draws it.
findings.evidence: guides.render_guide's sword() (lib/guides.py:120-132) draws the light blade with a crossguard in every frame, held or dropped. The ogre's --check-guides sheet, which I rendered and then deleted, shows a white sword in every strike, flinch and death cell, not a club. The sentence implies that only death 4–7 differ from the unit's weapon.
findings.fix: "the guide draws every weapon as a light sword blade with a crossguard, held and dropped (death 4–7); that is expected, and every text that shows the weapon must name it (club, hoe, greatsword) so the model draws it."

findings.quote: "unit": "swordsman" (final_hyborem_v1 strike/idle/death manifests); "facing": "lower-left" (swordsman_judged.json)
findings.evidence: The manifests in final_hyborem_v1/ and final_hyborem_v1_nofx/ name the unit 'swordsman', but units/hyborem_v1.json has name 'hyborem'. The engine contract (ANIMATING_UNITS.md:49, :65) says manifests carry `unit` and `facing`. Separately, units/swordsman_judged.json records facing 'lower-left' for a sprite that looks lower-right, though recipe.py's docstring defines facing as 'the way the sprite looks'. Its _note explains that it is legacy. These are legacy sets, so the impact is low, but they contradict the stated contract.
findings.fix: Re-cut the manifests (or fix the `unit` field) so final_hyborem_v1*/ say "hyborem", and add to the guide's legacy bullet (:377-379): "their manifests predate the `facing` field, and `swordsman_judged.json`'s `facing` is the direction it strikes, not where he looks."
